text: Hello, and welcome to this week's update from Project Parallax. Before the news, a question to carry with you. What if the universe is a kind of network that, in some sense, thinks? What would we measure to find out, and what result would count as a no? That is a thought, not a finding. Now, what is actually known. Nothing changed this week, so here is where things stand. First, near-death experiences, and whether the mind can work without the brain. Three of the six checks are fully met, and one more is partly met. Next, ancient stone building and its acoustics. None of the six checks are fully met, and four more are partly met. Then, cycles of catastrophe and the wobble of the Earth's axis. None of the six checks are fully met, and three more are partly met. Last, the comparison between brain networks and the cosmic web. One of the six checks is fully met, and two more are partly met. We also collect personal stories of near-death experiences. There are about 300 so far. They are people's own reports, not proof, and none have been independently confirmed. What this gives you: A quiet week is normal. Good evidence moves slowly, and nothing here changes without a reason. One thing to remember. These numbers show how much has been checked, not whether something is true. Open the Tribunal page on the website to see the details for yourself. Thanks for listening.
